record.field:
ODINS (Wiclouds) · Odoo Integration

1) Connection (Remote Control)

Type: REST · Base URL: https://wiclouds.es

connection_params (JSON):

{
  "token": ""
}
  • Authentication is done via header: x-access-token: <token>.
  • The token must be obtained from the ODINS/Wiclouds platform and configured in connection_params.

2) Available Procedures

The following predefined procedures are included in this module:

  • ODINS: Get Devices → discovers all available entities/devices from the platform and generates a structured JSON file for importing devices and sensors into Odoo.
  • ODINS: Get Sensor Readings → builds sensor plan and downloads readings from configured sensors for synchronization.

3) Typical Workflow

  1. Get Devices → calls GET /backend/v2/entities/ to discover available devices and their sensors, then generates a structured JSON file.
  2. Get Devices (Plan) → builds bag["sensors_plan"] with (sensor_id, device_parameter, sensor_parameter, level, dates).
  3. Get Sensor Readings → executes: GET /backend/STH/v1/contextEntities/type/Device/id/{device_id}/attributes/{sensor_id}?dateFrom=YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ&dateTo=YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ for each sensor in the plan and updates readings in Odoo.

4) Authentication

Required header:

x-access-token: <token>

The token is a JWT token that must be configured in the connection_params JSON field.

5) Odoo Configuration

In Device (mdm.measurement.device):

{
  "device_id": "Mex03:00000",
  "start_date": "2025-01-01"
}
  • device_id: ODINS device ID (format: Mex03:XXXXX)
  • start_date: Default start date if the sensor has no readings

In Sensor (mdm.measurement.device.sensor):

{
  "sensor_id": "Temperature",
  "level": "0", (optional)
  "start_date": "2025-01-01"
}
  • sensor_id: Full sensor ID from ODINS response (e.g., pulseCounter, Temperature)
  • level: For array sensors, specify the array index (0-7). For single value sensors, leave empty.
  • start_date: Overrides the device start date if provided

6) Endpoints Used

  • GET /backend/v2/entities/ → list all available entities/devices and their sensor structure
  • GET /backend/STH/v1/contextEntities/type/Device/id/{device_id}/attributes/{sensor_id} → get historical readings for a specific sensor
  • Query parameters: dateFrom and dateTo in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ)

7) API Response Structure

Device list response:

{
  "id": "Mex03:00000",
  "type": "Device",
  "batteryLevel": {"value": 85},
  "Temperature": {
    "type": "StructuredValue",
    "value": ["15.49", "16.65", "17.2", "17.71", "18.23", "18.5", "18.8", "19.06"]
  }
}

Sensor readings response:

{
  "contextResponses": [{
    "contextElement": {
      "attributes": [{
        "values": [{
          "recvTime": "2025-11-01T23:30:00.000Z",
          "attrValue": ["15.49", "16.65", "17.2", "17.71", "18.23", "18.5", "18.8", "19.06"]
        }]
      }]
    }
  }]
}

8) Important Notes

  • Array sensors: Multi-level sensors (Temperature, Humidity, Salinity) contain arrays with up to 8 values (indices 0-7)
  • Level configuration: Use numeric index (0, 1, 2, ..., 7) to select which array position to read
  • Timestamp format: API returns ISO format (2025-11-01T23:30:00.000Z), converted to Odoo format (2025-11-01 23:30:00)
  • Dynamic sensor IDs: Sensor keys include unique MongoDB-style IDs (e.g., Temperature)
  • Data validation: Module handles missing values, type conversions, and timestamp parsing errors gracefully

9) Configuration Examples

Single value sensor (pulseCounter):

Device: {"device_id": "Mex03:00000"}
Sensor: {"sensor_id": "pulseCounter"}

Array sensor (Temperature level 0):

Device: {"device_id": "Mex03:00000"}
Sensor: {"sensor_id": "Temperature", "level": "0"}

Array sensor (Temperature level 3):

Device: {"device_id": "Mex03:00000"}
Sensor: {"sensor_id": "Temperature", "level": "3"}

10) JSON Export Structure

The "Get Devices" procedure generates a structured JSON file: odins_devices_sensors_YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.json

JSON Structure:

{
  "procedure": "ODINS: Get Devices (All)",
  "executed_at": "2025-11-06 10:30:00",
  "summary": {
    "total_devices": 2,
    "total_sensors": 8,
    "total_api_entities": 2
  },
  "devices": [
    {
      "odins_id": "Mex03:00000",
      "name": "DISPOSITIVO",
      "serial_number": "0006800015",
      "sensors": [
        {
          "sensor_id": "batteryLevel",
          "type": "Integer",
          "unit_of_measure": "%",
          "has_levels": false
        },
        {
          "sensor_id": "pulseCounter",
          "type": "Float",
          "unit_of_measure": "L",
          "has_levels": false
        },
        {
          "sensor_id": "Temperature",
          "type": "StructuredValue",
          "unit_of_measure": "°C",
          "has_levels": true,
          "levels": {
            "0": 12.67,
            "1": 14.38,
            "2": 15.62
          }
        },
        {
          "sensor_id": "Humidity",
          "type": "StructuredValue",
          "unit_of_measure": "%",
          "has_levels": true,
          "levels": {
            "0": 44.42,
            "1": 54.4,
            "2": 52.58
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Usage:

  • Download the JSON file from remotecontrol attachments
  • Parse the JSON to extract device and sensor information
  • Create necessary sensor types and UOMs in Odoo
  • Use the structured data to prepare CSV imports or create records programmatically
  • For array sensors, each level contains complete configuration for separate sensor creation

13) Sensor Types Available

ODINS devices can have multiple sensor types:

  • pulseCounter_*: Pulse counters (e.g., water meters)
    • Properties: value, multiplier, unitCode (L, m³, etc.)
    • Typical use: Water consumption tracking
  • analogInput_*: Analog inputs (voltage, current, etc.)
    • Properties: value, formula, unitCode
    • Typical use: Battery voltage, pressure sensors
  • Temperature: Temperature sensors
    • StructuredValue array with up to 8 levels (indices 0-7)
    • unitCode: ºC
    • Typical use: Soil temperature at different depths
    • Example: ["15.49", "16.65", "17.2", "17.71", "18.23", "18.5", "18.8", "19.06"]
  • Humidity: Humidity sensors
    • StructuredValue array with up to 8 levels (indices 0-7)
    • unitCode: mm or % depending on configuration
    • Typical use: Soil moisture at different depths
  • Salinity: Salinity sensors
    • StructuredValue array with up to 8 levels (indices 0-7)
    • Typical use: Soil salinity monitoring
